newsitem.title: USA: UN sanctions head says Iraq oil sales wait aid nod.
newsitem.headline: UN sanctions head says Iraq oil sales wait aid nod.

text.p: U.N. Sanctions Committee on Iraq chairman Antonio Monteiro Wednesday said Baghdad would submit a new pricing formula for oil sales under the "oil-for-food" deal after a distribution plan was agreed upon.

Monteiro reiterated statements made earlier Wednesday by Iraqi Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon, who said Iraq did not see any political problems in restarting oil sales, but instead was awaiting procedures to be worked out for implementing a new distribution plan.

"I talked to the Iraqi ambassador at lunchtime, and what he told me is that Iraqi authorities are waiting for the mission of the the Secretariat to go there and establish the new distribution plan. And after this agreement the Iraqi government will immediately publish and tell us the new pricing list," Monteiro said.
The distribution plan was expected to be completed by June 30, and likely allow new oil contract processing shortly thereafter, U.N. officials said.
Monteiro, speaking after a meeting of the sanctions panel, said arranging the distribution plan, and receiving the new pricing formula, was a routine procedure.

Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude oil for a 180-day period in order to buy food and medicine for civilians suffering from sanctions slapped on Baghdad after the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The new round of oil sales was approved by the U.N. Security Council last week, and went into effect from June 8. The first period of sales ran from December to June.
